reason: The cited evidence confirms Cr/V precipitation in the baseline alloy (E4) and that a quinary RHEA design can suppress precipitation (E1), but no evidence is provided to support the specific mechanistic claims about Hf's effects on lattice distortion, defect trapping, or recombination, nor the prediction of retained negligible hardening.
premises: W38Ta36Cr15V11 forms Cr/V-rich precipitates under irradiation at ~1073 K
Hf addition increases lattice distortion and alters defect migration kinetics
Hf atoms act as effective trapping sites for radiation-induced point defects, enhancing recombination
Enhanced defect recombination inhibits nucleation and growth of Cr/V-rich precipitates
